audit.whatIsWrong: Rows 0-3 disagreed across layers: phases[].side read Lissandra on all seven rows while content win[] and packet.levelChart read Skill through level 5.
audit.why: Fizz has kill pressure from level 2 with Urchin Strike into Seastone Trident and takes flat reduced damage from every source; Lissandra's edge only starts when Frozen Tomb answers the shark. Levels 1-5 are even.
audit.corrected: Rows 0-3 moved to Skill as one atomic group, with the two whys claiming a Lissandra advantage rewritten.

audit.whatIsWrong: Playful / Trickster is called matchup-defining throughout but its cooldown never appears; it halves from 16s at rank 1 to 8s at rank 5.
audit.why: The whole 'bait it then commit' plan depends on how long the window lasts, and it shrinks by half over the laning phase.
audit.corrected: 16s-to-8s stated in breakdown.cooldowns, ahead and phases[3].why so the punish window is a real number.

audit.whatIsWrong: The page never said that Playful / Trickster and Chum the Waters both GROUND. Lissandra's E is a dash — grounding denies it — so the claw she is told to escape with is exactly the tool his kit turns off.
audit.why: Both abilities carry the grounding flag in the kit, and Riot's R text plus the pole's zone are the two moments Lissandra most wants to leave. Also unstated: Seastone Trident is an auto-attack reset, so the wind-up, not a cast, is the tell (missingInteractions autoreset-burst-tell).
audit.corrected: Grounding named in breakdown.cooldowns, enemyWin, the claw-out Do and the chase Don't; the W reset named as the burst tell.

audit.why: It is the field that carries real cooldowns.
audit.corrected: Playful / Trickster 16s to 8s, Chum the Waters 120s, Frozen Tomb 120s stated.

audit.whatIsWrong: dosFull[1].d was tradeGood verbatim, dontsFull[2].d was tradeBad verbatim, and dosFull[0].d ended with a duplicated 'Bait it, count it, then go' tacked onto a sentence that already said to bait it.
audit.corrected: Four bullet bodies rewritten to answer their own titles from Fizz's real ranges and cooldowns.

edits.before: Q-shatter the wave and chip his melee step-ups — your early Q harass is better than the lane gives it credit for.
edits.after: Level 1 is even: he wants melee range for Seastone Trident, you Q-shatter at 725 — neither converts a trade.

edits.before: Lost Chapter timing — Q spam stops hurting your mana. Chip Fizz every time he touches the wave.
edits.after: Even: Playful is 16s at rank 1, so he dodges one commit, and you farm around exactly that.

edits.before: - Fizz Playful / Trickster: matchup-defining — The untargetable hop dodges your whole combo — bait it before spending your burst. Read it like a second minimap. - Guard your R Frozen Tomb (self-cast) like a fifth summoner spell. - Ultimate goes to kill windows only.
edits.after: - Playful / Trickster is 16s at rank 1, 8s at rank 5 — it goes untargetable AND grounds you, so your claw cannot leave while his pole is out. - Chum the Waters is 120s at rank 1. - Frozen Tomb is 120s and belongs to his commit, never to poke.

edits.before: Fizz wins by landing Playful / Trickster, denying your pattern, and cashing the all-in before your pattern matures.
edits.after: Fizz wins by sticking Chum the Waters on you, grounding your claw, and hopping untargetable through the answer you spent.

edits.before: Ahead, hunt: claw into every river skirmish first, tomb the carry, and snowball picks — Fizz farming under tower can't stop a roaming Lissandra.
edits.after: Ahead, punish the pole: Playful is 16s at rank 1, so trade the second it lands and take every wave he cannot contest without it.

edits.before: Carry through picks — claw-root-tomb converts vision into kills better than any control mage; the map shrinks every time your E is up.
edits.after: Carry by holding the tomb for his commit — Fizz has one entry, and once the shark is on you at 550 the fight is one he loses.

edits.before: The untargetable hop dodges your whole combo — bait it before spending your burst. Bait it, count it, then go.
edits.after: Seastone Trident empowers his next attack — the wind-up, not the cast, is your cue to be inside W range.

edits.before: Q-shatter his wave contact, and when he steps to punish, W-root into full rotation and walk — the root tax makes every aggressive step expensive.
edits.after: Dark ice makes you untargetable and invulnerable while the shark erupts — come out of it and root him before Urchin Strike is back on 8s.

edits.before: Fizz burns Playful / Trickster on nothing — take the fifteen-second invitation.
edits.after: Your claw is 1050 range on 24s — his E grounds it, so leave before the pole.

edits.before: The claw is your entrance AND your exit — spending both directions on one greedy play is how Lissandras die famous.
edits.after: A 120s Frozen Tomb spent on Seastone Trident chip leaves you nothing for the shark that actually kills you.

edits.before: Clawing in with W on cooldown 'to poke' — an engage tool spent on chip damage is a Lissandra standing in melee range with no ice left.
edits.after: Chum the Waters grounds you and Playful takes him untargetable, so chasing past your claw means fighting him on his terms.

notes: Content win[0..6] already matched packet.levelChart, so only the stale full-layer sides moved; no win[N] twin edits existed to make. Ratings left alone. Not asserted: whether Lissandra's self-R untargetability removes an already-attached Chum the Waters fish, whether the shark's knockup can be avoided by casting dark ice after it attaches, and whether Playful's grounding blocks the claw's RE-activation (the return teleport) as well as the initial cast — none of that is in Riot's text, and the kit's needsResearch is empty by design.
